name: Printing the Squares of Numbers Within a Specified Range (Case 1)
description: Construct a program to write out the squares of even positive integers less than or equal to 10.

comments.content:
We need to repeat the same process for each of the even positive integers that are less than or equal to 10. To do this, we need to use a loop structure. We use for loops instead of a while loop because we need to repeat the loop a certain number of times, and for loops are best-suited in cases like this when we know ahead of time the number of times that we need to repeat the loop. Here, we want the for loop to start counting from 2 (2 is the first positive even number) with every even integer number up to (including) 10.

To do this, we initialize variable num to 2, loop until reaching 10 (inclusive), and increment num by 2 after each iteration of the loop.

In the first part of the loop header, we define a control variable num and initialize it to 2. In the second part of the loop header, we test whether the control variable has reached the termination threshold. The loop is repeated if the control variable is less than or equal to 10 and terminates when the control variable reaches 11. In the third part of the loop header, we increment the control variable by 2 after each iteration of the loop (because we want to print only every even integer numbers).

Note that the first part is executed once before the loop starts, the second part is executed before each iteration, and the third part is executed after each iteration of the loop. Also note that the += operator adds the value on the the right-hand side of the assignment operator (i.e., 2) to the current value of the variable on the left-hand side (i.e., value of variable num) and that value is stored in the variable num. Thus, this statement is equivalent to the statement num = num + 2.

In each iteration of the loop, this statement prints the square number to the default standard output stream. To square each number in the sequence, we multiply it by itself using the multiplication (*) operator.

Note that we do not necessarily have to store the squared number in a variable. The multiplication may also be performed directly in the println statement.
The expression in the argument of the println method returns a string that is obtained by concatenating the given string and value of the variables.
